name: HaDeS
description: HaDeS is a token-level, reference-free hallucination detection benchmark for free-form text generation. It provides fine-grained annotations to detect hallucinated content without relying on ground-truth references, addressing challenges in real-time hallucination detection.
reputation: A niche but well-regarded recent benchmark for fine-grained hallucination detection, mainly used in research on factuality and faithfulness evaluation rather than broad leaderboard tracking.
notes: Dataset created by perturbing Wikipedia text segments and verified with crowd-sourced annotations; uses an iterative model-in-loop strategy to mitigate label imbalance.
